title: OpenVPN: The Flexible Veteran That Censors Can Fingerprint
metaTitle: What Is OpenVPN? How It Works and Why ISPs Can Detect It
metaDescription: OpenVPN explained: how its TLS control channel and data channel work, why it is slower than WireGuard, and why research identified over 85% of OpenVPN flows on a real ISP.
excerpt: Two decades old, endlessly configurable and supported almost everywhere. Researchers also showed an ISP can pick out most OpenVPN traffic by its shape.

faq.question: Is OpenVPN still secure?
faq.answer: A current OpenVPN release with a sound configuration is secure. Because it is so configurable, the main risk is a weak setup, such as outdated ciphers, rather than a flaw in the protocol.

faq.question: Why is OpenVPN detected even on port 443?
faq.answer: Using port 443 does not make the traffic look like HTTPS. OpenVPN frames its TLS handshake in its own packet format, and published research identified over 85% of OpenVPN flows on a real ISP network by that shape.

faq.question: OpenVPN or WireGuard?
faq.answer: On an open network WireGuard is usually faster and simpler. OpenVPN wins on compatibility and can run over TCP. Neither is designed to hide from censors.

faq.question: Is OpenVPN UDP or TCP?
faq.answer: Either. UDP is the default and is usually faster; TCP helps on networks that block UDP, at some cost in speed.
